page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning comprises 48.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring remote network storage solutions, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements position the ecs.c6.6xlarge predominantly in the middle tier of general cloud systems, accompanied by weaker single-threaded results. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 21,643.62 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,967.0, while single-core evaluations such as stress-ng (1313.3) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.86 GB/sec) placed in the lower 25%. Instruction extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support alongside AES-NI. Memory subsystems recorded an uncached read throughput of 108.94 GB/sec and uncached write throughput of 47.99 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 20.09 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 15.86 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The 1:2 memory allocation is cost-efficient for parallel CPU-bound tasks where excessive per-core RAM overhead is unnecessary. However, the absence of bundled local storage requires persistent cloud volumes, and moderate single-core speeds make it less optimal for serial workloads. This server profile is well matched for distributed batch computing, software compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
